tagline: Around the great circle of the Grande Ronde Valley.
intro: The loop leaves La Grande, whose name came from a phrase a Frenchman, Charles Dause, used for the scenery, and runs south along the base of the Blue Mountains past Ladd Marsh, then over a short gravel stretch by Hot Lake to Union. South of Union, Thief Valley Reservoir Road gives fifteen miles of gravel and open country before OR 203 climbs to Catherine Creek Summit and follows the creek back down.
From Union, OR 237 runs north to Cove, at the foot of Mount Fanny on the valley's eastern edge.
season: TripCheck gives spring through fall as the best time to visit.

moments.title: Hot Lake
moments.text: Oregon's largest hot spring heated the first known commercial building in the world to run mainly on geothermal energy, a sanatorium once called the Mayo Clinic of the West.

moments.title: Medical Springs
moments.text: Where Hot Lake drew wealthy travelers, this hot springs resort drew miners, gamblers and cowboys, and its founder, a cousin of Lincoln, lived here past his hundredth birthday.

moments.title: Cove
moments.text: The post office dropped the Forest from Forest Cove in 1868 to avoid confusion with Forest Grove, and Ascension Chapel, an Episcopal church, went up the next year.

practical: Mostly paved, with gravel by Hot Lake and for about 15 miles on Thief Valley Reservoir Road, and closed in bad weather.
